custom.message: An arbitrary Tailwind value (w-[37px], text-[11px], bg-[#0b0b0f]): use a token's utility, or add the token to packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css and theme.css. A custom property is written w-(--name), never w-[var(--name)] (MAR-3617; docs/checks/design-system-drift.md).

A colour value outside the tokens: every colour is a token in packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css (light-dark() for both themes), worn as a utility (bg-surface, text-danger-ink) or var(--name). Code that can't read CSS takes a mirror from @convergence/ui, as xterm takes terminalTokens (MAR-3617; DS-26).

A Tailwind palette colour (text-red-500, bg-emerald-500/10): a colour is a role, not a shade (R1). A status is one of five tones, neutral, info, success, warning and danger: text-<tone>-ink, bg-<tone>-soft, border-<tone>-line, bg-<tone>-solid, or the tone prop of Badge, StatusPill, StatusDot and Notice. A named category is a hue token: merged, crew-*, provider-*, tag-* (MAR-3617; DS-1).

A dark: class in app code: fix the colour in its token instead. Each token is light-dark(LIGHT, DARK) in packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css, so a utility is right in both themes by itself; dark: belongs inside @convergence/ui only (packages/ui/AGENTS.md; MAR-3617).

A white or black overlay (border-white/10, bg-black/20) assumes a dark surface and vanishes on a light one: use the theme-safe tokens, border-line-soft for a hairline, bg-fill-hover and bg-fill-selected for the hover and chosen fills, bg-fill-quiet for a faint panel, bg-chip for a chip (MAR-3617; DS-2).

A name only Streamdown's markup may write (bg-background, text-muted-foreground, border-border, bg-black…): theme.css's vendor bridge keeps it painting for Streamdown's bundle alone, and the app and the design system write the token: background -> canvas, foreground -> ink, muted -> surface-muted, muted-foreground -> ink-muted, border -> line (border/60 to /80 -> line-soft), sidebar -> surface-sunken, primary -> strong, primary-foreground -> on-strong, black -> viewer behind a picture or scrim behind a dialog; var(--color-muted) is var(--surface-muted) (MAR-3618; docs/checks/design-system-drift.md).

Motion by hand (duration-150, delay-75, transition-all): durations are the motion tokens, duration-exit, duration-fast, duration-panel and duration-slow (a bare transition is already duration-fast), and a transition names what moves (transition-colors, transition-opacity, transition-transform), never all (MAR-3617).

A focus ring typed by hand (focus-visible:outline-focus, focus-visible:ring-focus, or the old ring-ring): use focusRing, focusRingInset, focusRingField or focusRingWithin from @convergence/ui, which pick the ring by where the element sits (Button, IconButton, Input and TextLink have theirs). Copies drift, and in Tailwind 4 most typed outline rings draw nothing (MAR-3588; MAR-3617; MAR-3618; DS-7).

A focus ring that draws nothing: in Tailwind 4, outline-none sets the outline's style to none, and focus-visible:outline-2 draws in that style. Use focusRing (or a sibling) from @convergence/ui; if you must type it, add focus-visible:outline-solid (MAR-3588; MAR-3617).

A spinner built by hand: give the Button pending (with pendingLabel), or use Spinner from @convergence/ui. Both run on the motion tokens and stand still under reduced motion, and a pending Button keeps its width and sets aria-busy (MAR-3617; DS-12).
An error line built by hand: use FormError from @convergence/ui (FieldError inside a Field, DS3c), so every error reads, sits and is announced the same way (MAR-3617; DS-5, DS-13).

A native title on a button (R2): an icon-only button is an IconButton, whose label is its aria-label and its tooltip; anything else wears <Tooltip label>. The browser's title is slow, unstyled and never shows on focus (MAR-3617; DS-3).
A Button or IconButton resized in className: pick one of its sizes (R3), size="xs", "sm", "md" or "lg" (24, 28, 32 and 36 px). A height typed on top drifts from every other control (MAR-3617; DS-4).

The operating system's confirm box: ask in the app with ConfirmDialog (or useConfirm) from @convergence/ui (DS3b), variant="danger" when the action destroys something, so the question looks like Convergence and the focus starts on Cancel (R5; MAR-3617; DS-6).

A raw <button>, <a>, <input>, <textarea> or <select>: use the design system's part (Button, IconButton, buttonVariants on a link, TextLink, ListRow, Input, Textarea, Select…), or say why not on the line above: // raw-element: <reason>, or {/* raw-element: <reason> */} in JSX. Scoped to apps/convergence: it names Convergence's own design system, and Backpack Studio's is Backpack (MAR-2705; MAR-3617; DS-27). A raw <label>: FieldLabel in a Field, which wires the label, the hint and the error to the control, or ChoiceField around a Switch or a Checkbox (DS-13, DS-14).

Every @convergence/ui component and motion primitive (components/<name>/<name>.tsx, motion/<name>/<name>.tsx) ships <name>.stories.tsx beside it: the stories run as tests, with an axe check, in both themes (packages/ui/AGENTS.md).

Every presentational part has <name>.stories.tsx beside it. A sub-part drawn only inside a bigger part's stories is listed in this rule's exclude instead, one line per folder (docs/checks/design-system-drift.md; MAR-3617).
A stories file's meta title starts with one of the seven groups, in the sidebar's order: Foundations, Primitives, Components, Motion, Entities, Features, Widgets (packages/ui/AGENTS.md).
Every story runs as a test with an axe check that fails it (a11y: { test: 'error' }); 'todo' or 'off' switches the accessibility gate off for the whole design system.
